issues.legal_issue: The actual cost of an asset-related work should be accepted over a hypothetical estimate when reliable evidence from the person who performed the work, supported by a document, establishes the actual cost.
material_facts: A prosecution witness who was a public works engineer estimated the cost of excavating the well using public works data.
The person who carried out the work testified that the excavation cost less and produced a supporting document.
The prosecution had called that person, relied on his evidence, and had not treated him as hostile.
issues.conclusion: The actual expenditure established by the contractor’s testimony and document had to be accepted, and the excess amount included on the basis of the estimate had to be excluded.
issues.legal_principle: A prosecution cannot rely on one of its witnesses’ evidence while rejecting contradictory evidence from another prosecution witness whom it has not treated as hostile. A hypothetical estimate based on standard data cannot prevail over reliable evidence of the actual expenditure supported by a document.

rule.if: disproportionate_assets_appeal and prosecution_witness_gives_hypothetical_estimate and actual_contractor_evidence_is_documented and contractor_is_prosecution_witness and contractor_is_not_treated_as_hostile

predicates.disproportionate_assets_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal from a conviction for possessing assets disproportionate to known sources of income.
predicates.prosecution_witness_gives_hypothetical_e: A prosecution witness estimates the cost of work using standard data rather than knowledge of the actual expenditure.
predicates.actual_contractor_evidence_is_documented: The person who performed the work testifies to its actual cost and supports that testimony with a document.
predicates.contractor_is_prosecution_witness: The prosecution called the person who performed the work as a witness.
predicates.contractor_is_not_treated_as_hostile: The prosecution did not treat the person who performed the work as a hostile witness.

issues.definition: When a disproportionate-assets appeal involves a hypothetical estimate and documented actual-cost evidence from a prosecution witness whom the prosecution did not treat as hostile, the actual expenditure controls.

issues.legal_issue: A property held in a relative’s name cannot be treated as the accused’s benami property without definite legal evidence proving that the relative was not the real owner.
material_facts: The prosecution alleged that properties purchased in the accused’s father’s and wife’s names were actually the accused’s properties.
The father had been a schoolteacher, had retired, and had received provident-fund and gratuity payments around the time of one purchase.
The High Court found that the alleged benami transaction had not been proved beyond reasonable doubt but nevertheless included part of the purchase consideration in the asset calculation.
The Supreme Court found no basis for retaining that part of the consideration as an asset of the accused.
issues.conclusion: The alleged benami transaction was not established, and the amount included on that basis had to be excluded from the accused’s assets.
issues.legal_principle: Under Krishnanand Agnihotri v. State of M.P., the burden of proving a benami transaction rests on the person asserting it and must be strictly discharged by definite legal evidence that directly proves benami ownership or establishes circumstances unerringly supporting that inference. Conjecture or surmise is insufficient.

rule.if: disproportionate_assets_prosecution and property_is_held_in_relative_name and prosecution_asserts_accused_is_real_owner and relative_has_independent_financial_means and definite_legal_evidence_does_not_establish_benami_ownership

predicates.disproportionate_assets_prosecution: The proceeding is a prosecution alleging that an accused public servant possessed assets disproportionate to known sources of income.
predicates.property_is_held_in_relative_name: The property is recorded in the name of a relative of the accused.
predicates.prosecution_asserts_accused_is_real_owne: The prosecution alleges that the accused, rather than the named relative, is the real owner of the property.
predicates.relative_has_independent_financial_means: The named relative has evidence of independent resources that could support the purchase.
predicates.definite_legal_evidence_does_not_establi: The evidence does not directly prove benami ownership or establish circumstances that unerringly support that inference.

issues.definition: If property is held in a relative’s name, the prosecution alleges the accused is the real owner, the relative has independent means, and definite legal evidence does not establish benami ownership, benami ownership is not established.

issues.legal_issue: Supported net income from leased agricultural land must be included when determining an accused’s known sources of income.
material_facts: The accused claimed income from leased agricultural land.
The lower courts had found the land area and income per acre, and the calculation accounted for lease rent.
The courts had allowed a lower amount of income than the net amount supported by those findings and the rent calculation.
The Supreme Court’s rejection of the benami finding meant that the relevant income was attributable to the accused.
issues.conclusion: The supported net income from the leased land had to be added to the accused’s total income.
issues.legal_principle: In assessing whether assets are disproportionate to known sources of income, income supported by the findings on the leased land and the associated rent must be credited to the accused’s income.

predicates.disproportionate_assets_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal from a conviction for possessing assets disproportionate to known sources of income.
predicates.accused_claims_income_from_leased_land: The accused claims income derived from land held under a lease.
predicates.evidence_supports_lease_income_and_expen: The evidence supports both the income derived from the leased land and the expenses paid for the lease.
predicates.allowed_income_is_less_than_supported_ne: The amount credited by the lower court is less than the net income supported by the evidence.

issues.definition: When a disproportionate-assets appeal concerns claimed income from leased land and the evidence supports a higher net amount than the lower court allowed, the supported net lease income is added to known income.

issues.legal_issue: Income from the sale of agricultural produce must be included in known income when the evidence supports that the produce was grown and there is no evidence that the land yielded only fodder.
material_facts: The accused claimed income from the sale of pulses grown on agricultural land.
The evidence indicated that pulses were produced on the land.
The lower courts rejected the claim as though the crop were fodder, although there was no evidence that it was fodder.
issues.conclusion: The claimed income from the sale of pulses had to be added to the accused’s total income.
issues.legal_principle: Income supported by evidence of agricultural production cannot be rejected on the unsupported assumption that the land produced only fodder.

predicates.disproportionate_assets_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal from a conviction for possessing assets disproportionate to known sources of income.
predicates.accused_claims_income_from_agricultural_: The accused claims income from the sale of produce grown on agricultural land.
predicates.evidence_supports_production_of_saleable: The evidence supports that the land produced a crop capable of sale.
predicates.no_evidence_shows_only_fodder_was_produc: There is no evidence that the land produced only fodder.

issues.definition: When a disproportionate-assets appeal involves a supported claim of income from a saleable crop and no evidence that only fodder was produced, the supported crop-sale income is added to known income.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for possessing assets disproportionate to known sources of income cannot stand when the corrected accounting shows no excess assets and the prosecution has not satisfactorily established disproportion.
material_facts: The High Court had found a value of disproportionate assets, but the Supreme Court excluded unsupported asset amounts and credited supported income.
After those corrections, the accused’s income exceeded the value of the assets even without applying any additional margin.
The Supreme Court concluded that the prosecution had not satisfactorily established that the accused held assets disproportionate to known sources of income.
issues.conclusion: The conviction and sentence were set aside, the appeal was allowed, and any fine already paid was ordered to be refunded.
issues.legal_principle: For an offence under Sections 5(1)(e) and 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, the prosecution must satisfactorily establish that the public servant possessed assets disproportionate to known sources of income. Where the properly assessed income accounts for the assets, the conviction cannot be sustained.

predicates.appeal_against_disproportionate_assets_c: The proceeding is an appeal against a conviction for possessing assets disproportionate to known sources of income.
predicates.corrected_accounting_shows_no_excess_ass: After correcting the asset and income calculations, the accused’s known income is sufficient to account for the assets.
predicates.prosecution_does_not_satisfactorily_esta: The prosecution has not satisfactorily established that the accused’s assets exceed known sources of income.

issues.definition: If an appeal against a disproportionate-assets conviction results in corrected accounting showing no excess assets and the prosecution has not satisfactorily established disproportion, the conviction is set aside and an acquittal is ordered.
